result.description: CRM platform for marketing, sales, service, content and operations, with a broad public API for CRM objects and more.
result.auth_detail: OAuth2 for apps distributed to multiple accounts (required for marketplace). Static auth (service keys / legacy private-app bearer tokens) for a single account. Developer API key only for app settings such as webhooks. Standard hapikeys were retired in 2022. New legacy private apps cannot be created after 2026-10-26.
result.access_detail: Developer account and OAuth app creation are free and self-serve. Free and Starter accounts have API rate limits, per the private apps page. Marketplace listing is optional and not needed for end users to connect. Doc pages I fetched say nothing on free-account or developer-account self-serve signup, so the free-signup claim comes from general knowledge, not a page quote. Access confidence is medium.
result.api_notes: REST at api.hubapi.com with date-based versioning (e.g. /crm/2026-09/). Covers CRM objects, engagements, marketing, CMS, conversations, webhooks and more. Official SDKs exist. I did not count endpoints. "Broad" rests on the date-versioned CRM reference and general knowledge.

evidence.quote: If you plan to distribute your app to multiple accounts (either through listing on the HubSpot Marketplace or by managing specific authorized accounts), your app must be built using OAuth authentication.
As of October 26, 2026, legacy private apps can no longer be created.
You must be a super admin to access private apps in your HubSpot account.
The 2026-09 APIs use a date-based versioning scheme (e.g., `/crm/2026-09/`).
All APIs, whether legacy, new, or beta, use the same root path as before: `https://api.hubapi.com/`.
PKCE is required for authenticating with HubSpot's MCP server.
